structured.lead: The rhyme scheme of the Spenserian sonnet is
structured.options_hint: abab bcbc cdcd ee abab cdcd efef gg abba

items.explanation: Developed by Edmund Spenser for his sonnet sequence Amoretti (1595), the Spenserian sonnet consists of three interlocking quatrains and a final rhyming couplet with the linked rhyme scheme abab bcbc cdcd ee.

items.explanation: Barabas, the wealthy merchant protagonist of Christopher Marlowe's play The Jew of Malta (c. 1589–1590), is consumed by avarice and material greed, famously celebrating 'Infinite riches in a little room.'

structured.lead: The term, 'curtal sonnet', was coined by
structured.options_hint: John Milton William Blake Gerald Manley

items.explanation: Victorian poet Gerard Manley Hopkins coined the term 'curtal sonnet' in the preface to his poems to describe his curtailed 10.5-line sonnet form, which he used in poems such as 'Pied Beauty' and 'Peace.'

structured.lead: Thomas Kyd's The Spanish Tragedy was influenced by
structured.options_hint: Seneca Tertullian Virgil Plautus

items.explanation: Thomas Kyd's Elizabethan revenge play The Spanish Tragedy (c. 1587) was heavily influenced by the Roman stoic tragedian Seneca, adopting Senecan devices such as a vengeful ghost, a chorus (Revenge), stichomythia, and onstage bloodshed.

structured.lead: Hamlet, lying wounded, says to his friend, "Horatio, I am dead." This is an example of
structured.options_hint: protasis anacrusis prolepsis pun

items.explanation: When the mortally wounded Hamlet tells Horatio 'I am dead' in Act V, Scene ii before actually dying, he uses prolepsis—a rhetorical figure in which a future event or state is spoken of as if it has already occurred.

items.explanation: Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto (1764), subtitled 'A Gothic Story' in its second edition, is universally recognized as the first English Gothic novel, establishing conventions of haunted castles, ancestral curses, and supernatural terror.

items.explanation: 'The City of Dreadful Night' (1874) was written by Scottish-born Victorian poet James Thomson under the pseudonym 'B.V.' (Bysshe Vanolis). The bleak, pessimistic poem portrays a nightmare metropolis of urban alienation and existential despair.

structured.options_hint: eliminates the ego promotes sensuality d

items.explanation: In Book X of The Republic, Plato censured poetry through his theory of mimesis, arguing that because the physical world is already an imperfect copy of ideal Forms, poetic imitation is 'thrice removed from truth' and distorts reality.

items.explanation: Andrew Marvell composed 'An Horatian Ode upon Cromwell's Return from Ireland' in the summer of 1650, immediately following Oliver Cromwell's return from his Irish campaign in May 1650 and before his invasion of Scotland.

items.explanation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge's ballad 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner' (1798) centres on the spiritual crime, psychological guilt, penance, and ongoing expiation of the Mariner after he wantonly shoots the auspicious Albatross.

structured.lead: "To Daffodils" is a poem, written by
structured.options_hint: Robert Herrick William Wordsworth John K

items.explanation: 'To Daffodils' ('Fair Daffodils, we weep to see / You haste away so soon') is a lyric poem on the brevity of human life by Cavalier poet Robert Herrick, published in his collection Hesperides (1648).

structured.lead: Which of the following novels reconstructs the historical events of the Indian Mutiny ?
structured.options_hint: The Jewel in the Crown The Siege of Kris

items.explanation: J. G. Farrell's Booker Prize-winning novel The Siege of Krishnapur (1973) reconstructs the 1857 Indian Mutiny through the fictionalized siege of a British residency town, whereas the other three novels belong to Paul Scott's Raj Quartet set in the 1940s.

items.explanation: 'England, My England' (originally titled 'Pro Rege Nostro') is a famous patriotic poem written by late-Victorian poet William Ernest Henley and published in The Song of the Sword and Other Verses (1892).

items.explanation: Percy Bysshe Shelley and his friend Thomas Jefferson Hogg were expelled from University College, Oxford, in March 1811 after refusing to disavow authorship of their anonymously printed rationalist pamphlet The Necessity of Atheism.
